validation.notes: The regression passes on the repaired tree and fails with a plain node:assert/strict AssertionError (no crash, import error or timeout) when any single repaired file is restored to its faulty baseline: runtime/drive/tools.ts -> 'unsafe persisted declaration: the tool effect must not run'; execution/tools.ts -> 'the executor must run with the cleared/persisted arguments'; execution/effect-gate.ts -> 'an aborting gate must refuse admission'. The script loads the real modules through .prale-eval/subject.mjs (real drive -> real tool executor -> real effect gate, only checkpoint storage, progress transport and provider/hook delivery faked) and asserts across module boundaries: (1) both replay declarations must be safe, so a persisted-safe call behind a replay:"never" tool, a persisted-never call behind a replay:"safe" tool, and a missing tool are never admitted and keep their durable checkpoint evidence; (2) the executor receives the cleared/persisted arguments {message:'persisted-arguments'} rather than the model arguments {message:'raw-model-arguments'}, and runs under the gate's own AbortSignal with the drive-built invocation identity; (3) the old checkpoint is cleared before invocation and the outcome is published only after the external effect completed and progress.drain() finished, verified with promise-controlled effect and drain gates (no timers, randomness or external services); (4) cancellation and an aborting gate refuse admission with the invocation published as interrupted after the drain, and a closed gate rejects with its own closing error; direct gate checks confirm admit() is state aware (closed throws the closing error without running the work, aborting throws AbortRequested carrying the cancellation promise, open admits synchronously). Limitation: the repository's vitest suites and the TypeScript type check could not be executed because node_modules/dependencies are not installed in this workspace; the standalone Node 24 vm-module script is the focused validation and needs no dependencies.
